claims.head: Where the Oilers have the edge: the power play
claims.body: The Oilers are the league’s best for the power play, and the Ducks are around the middle. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays, and Anaheim’s power play has been near the bottom of the league for years.

claims.body: The Ducks are around the middle of the league for depth, and the Oilers are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.

ANA.head: A slightly uphill night for the Ducks
ANA.body: Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents lately, but Anaheim has home-ice advantage. The Ducks’ best way to tip it is getting good looks.

EDM.head: The Oilers have a slight edge
EDM.body: Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents lately, but Anaheim has home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Ducks can make it interesting if they get good looks.

items.text: Evan Bouchard has a point in eleven straight games against Anaheim.
First meeting since the Ducks beat the Oilers in six games in last spring’s first round.
The Oilers have been without Zach Hyman, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Matt Savoie all season.
The Ducks have been without Troy Terry and Drew Helleson all season. Counting how much each missing player usually brings, only the Islanders are missing more right now.
